questions.prompt: Name the star at the centre of our solar system.
questions.answer: The Sun.

questions.prompt: Define a natural satellite.
questions.answer: A moon that orbits a planet.

questions.prompt: Name the galaxy that our solar system is part of.
questions.answer: The Milky Way.

questions.prompt: Define the solar system.
questions.answer: The Sun (one star), the eight planets and the dwarf planets that orbit it, plus the natural satellites (moons) that orbit planets.

questions.prompt: Define a nebula.
questions.answer: A cloud of dust and gas.

title: Formation of the Sun and stars

questions.prompt: State what the Sun was formed from.
questions.answer: A cloud of dust and gas (a nebula) pulled together by gravitational attraction.

questions.prompt: State what causes fusion reactions to start at the beginning of a star's life cycle.
questions.answer: Gravity pulling the dust and gas together heats the core until fusion begins.

questions.prompt: State what balances the gravitational collapse of a star.
questions.answer: The outward pressure from the energy released by fusion reactions.

questions.prompt: State what determines the life cycle of a star.
questions.answer: Its size (mass).

questions.prompt: State where elements heavier than iron are produced.
questions.answer: In a supernova (the explosion of a massive star).

questions.prompt: State the process that produces the naturally occurring elements in stars.
questions.answer: Nuclear fusion.

questions.prompt: Define a supernova.
questions.answer: The explosion of a massive star, which distributes elements throughout the universe.

questions.prompt: State the force that keeps planets and satellites in their orbits.
questions.answer: Gravity.

questions.prompt: State how the velocity of an object in a circular orbit changes when its speed is constant.
questions.answer: Its velocity changes, because its direction changes.

questions.prompt: Name a natural satellite of the Earth and an artificial satellite.
questions.answer: The Moon; any man-made satellite (e.g. a communications satellite).

questions.prompt: Define an artificial satellite.
questions.answer: A man-made object that orbits a planet.

questions.prompt: Define red-shift.
questions.answer: The increase in the observed wavelength of light from distant, receding galaxies.

questions.prompt: State what red-shift provides evidence for.
questions.answer: An expanding universe, which supports the Big Bang theory.

questions.prompt: State what the Big Bang theory suggests about the early universe.
questions.answer: The universe began from a very small, extremely hot and dense region.

questions.prompt: State how the red-shift of a galaxy changes with its distance from us.
questions.answer: The further away the galaxy, the faster it is moving away and the bigger the observed increase in wavelength.

questions.prompt: State what observations of supernovae since 1998 suggest about distant galaxies.
questions.answer: They are receding ever faster.

questions.prompt: Name two things about the universe that are still not understood.
questions.answer: Dark mass (dark matter) and dark energy.
